fields.description:
## Context / Problem
An indeterminate plan review can contain expensive successful calls plus a small retryable coverage gap. A normal rerun repeats everything, while blindly resuming old checkpoints risks applying results to changed material or policy. The maintainer approved an explicit `rebar review-plan --retry` override that resumes only the literal latest eligible review and authorizes a fresh attempt budget.

## Approach
Add CLI parsing and a narrow library-internal retry request. Eligibility is read from the latest retained `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar payload (`sidecar.latest_review_result`): its embedded reducer-ignored `discovery_journal` enumerates the units of that exact review and their per-unit outcomes (success/resumed/skipped/shed/failed), and the verdict must be `INDETERMINATE` with at least one retryable missing unit. **The journal is content-free — it is used only to identify the latest review, enumerate its units, and classify each unit as reusable vs missing; it is never the source of finding content.** The reusable *content* of each successful/resumed unit is reconstructed from the chunk-atomic `CheckpointEnvelope`s written by `sizing.save_checkpoint`: for each such unit the retry recomputes its `checkpoint_identity` / `identity_digest` from the current ticket material, code/ref, effective policy, prompts/contracts, model/mode, topology, context, dependencies, and source, then loads the envelope via `sizing.load_checkpoint(ctx, digest)` and reuses its stored `findings` — exactly the resume join `pass1` already performs. A unit whose recomputed digest matches no stored envelope (changed material/policy/etc.), or whose envelope is absent, is NOT reusable: it is treated as missing and re-run (a budget-shed unit stays missing). Assembled prior verdict fields (`findings`, `coverage`) come from that same sidecar `build_payload`. This retry layers ONLY a latest-review eligibility gate and a fresh attempt budget over the existing chunk-checkpoint resume seam — it introduces no second resume mechanism. The lineage must be digest-complete and content-identical across ticket material, code/ref, effective policy, prompts/contracts, model/mode, topology, context, dependencies, and source. Legacy `REVIEW_RESULT` payloads without the versioned `discovery_journal`, and legacy (pre-namespace) checkpoints, never seed retry.

Reuse every eligible successful unit's checkpointed findings, including clean and blocking results, and issue model calls only for missing units. Budget-shed units remain missing. Pass-2 verification and coaching reuse unchanged per-finding successes and run only for newly recovered work; deterministic decision, assembly, signature eligibility, and narrow response rendering rerun over the combined result. Each explicit `--retry` grants a fresh per-invocation attempt budget. Cumulative lineage spend is stored as audit telemetry and never blocks a later explicit retry.

Fail before any model call when the latest result is not eligible or when its journal is missing, **stale** (the latest sidecar/journal no longer reflects current lineage: its recomputed identity-digest set no longer matches the present material / effective policy / prompts / contracts / model / mode / topology / context / dependencies / source, so no successful unit's checkpoint can be validly reused), corrupt, legacy, or digest-mismatched. Refusal is not a silent full review and gives the operator the normal full-review remedy. `--retry` is mutually exclusive with `--force`, `--status`, and `--check`; `--no-sign` remains compatible. Normal review behavior is unchanged without the flag.

`--retry` is a CLI / library operator affordance. The MCP `review_plan` tool mirror is intentionally out of scope for this story (retry is an interactive operator override, not an automated-caller path); the MCP surface keeps full-review semantics and the file impact deliberately excludes the MCP tool module. Retry is operation-linked (CLI plus in-process library) with no CI-provider dependency, so it is portable across environments with any CI provider or none.

Document the flag in the native canonical `review-plan --help`, generated `docs/cli-reference.md`, `docs/user-guide.md`, `docs/plan-review-gate.md`, and `docs/exit-codes.md`. Documentation must explain eligibility, fresh budget, reused blockers/successes, zero-call refusal, incompatible flags, signing behavior, and the distinction from `--status` and `sign-review`. Review and status responses remain narrow end-result views; the retry journal is not printed.

## Migration and Rollback
The flag is additive and opt-in. Older journals are deliberately ineligible, so rollout needs no data rewrite. Removing the CLI flag and retry reader restores full-review-only behavior while leaving reducer-ignored journals harmless. Normal review remains the documented fallback for any refusal.

## Testing
Use a real CLI subprocess with a temporary ticket store plus the production journal codec and stateful fake at the model boundary. Assert exit code, stdout/stderr contract, exact called unit ids, stored lineage, and final verdict. Fault and negative-control cases assert zero calls. A generated-help test proves the documented flag is derived from canonical help rather than hand-maintained drift.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Given a literal latest completed `INDETERMINATE` RP-06 journal with two successful units and one retryable missing unit, `rebar review-plan <id> --retry` calls only the missing unit and combines all three content-identical results.
- [ ] Clean and blocking successes are reusable, budget-shed units remain missing, verification/coaching call only for newly recovered findings, and deterministic decision/assembly reruns over the combined set.
- [ ] Each explicit retry receives the normal fresh per-invocation attempt budget; cumulative lineage usage is recorded but never enforced as a cap.
- [ ] A latest `PASS`/`BLOCK`, a non-retryable indeterminate result, or a missing, legacy, corrupt, stale, or digest-mismatched journal refuses before any model/provider call and never falls through to a full review.
- [ ] CLI contract tests prove `--retry` conflicts with `--force`, `--status`, and `--check`, remains compatible with `--no-sign`, and preserves normal no-flag behavior.
- [ ] Retry output and `review-plan --status` expose only established end-result fields and no per-unit execution trace or verbose journal details.
- [ ] Canonical `review-plan --help`, generated CLI reference, user guide, plan-review gate guide, and exit-code guide document eligibility, fresh budget, reuse/refusal behavior, flag interactions, signing, and the normal-full-review remedy.
- [ ] A real CLI subprocess test proves the eligible resume path, zero-call refusal path, persisted retry lineage, and final exit/verdict semantics end to end.
